sources.entry: Notch So Good - A pixel-art crab lives in your MacBook notch and monitors Claude Code sessions with 13 animations, smart notifications, and multi-session support.

summary.one_liner: A macOS menu-bar/notch app where a pixel-art crab called Peek sits beside the MacBook notch and monitors Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI sessions, letting you approve or answer agent prompts from the notch.
summary.what_it_does: Shows a black pill extending the notch with Peek on the left and a ring on the right showing remaining 5-hour usage. Peek animates to reflect agent state and climbs out further when a session needs attention. Finished tasks, errors and usage warnings open a card naming the project, and clicking it jumps to the terminal tab or tmux pane. When Claude Code asks for permission, the notch can show the full command or file diff with Allow, Deny, "This session" and "Always allow" options, plus question and plan answers and a reply box after a task finishes. Multiple sessions are listed on hover, and the app warns when two sessions edit the same file. The menu bar shows Claude Code and Codex usage windows and reset times, with heads-ups at 80%, 95% and when used up. Approvals use Claude Code's own PermissionRequest hook, and a local Unix socket bridge keeps data on the Mac.
use_cases: monitor Claude Code sessions while working elsewhere
approve or deny agent commands without switching windows
track Claude Code and Codex usage limits
get notified when a coding agent finishes a task
keep track of multiple concurrent AI coding sessions
reply to Claude Code from the menu bar
notable: Approvals come from Claude Code's own PermissionRequest hook, so cards appear only when the agent would ask anyway
Peek is an animated 3D pixel character with states and idle behaviours
Keyboard shortcuts (⌃⌥ plus A, D, S, 1–6, R, N, O) work while a card is up
Agent radar warns when two sessions edit the same file
Updates download in the background and wait for a restart
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later; the notch layout is best on a notched MacBook, with a fallback island on other Macs
Approval features need Claude Code 2.0.45+, and answering questions and plans needs 2.1.85+; reply-from-notch needs 2.1.287+
Gemini CLI support is beta and watching only
Not notarized by Apple; the installers clear the download quarantine flag
